note: Pre-Islamic poet; sources only give an approximate death ('nahw 20 years before the Hijra' ~= 603 CE); no firm scholarly date found, no AH year applicable (pre-Hijra).
Wikipedia and Britannica agree on 845 CE (231 AH), died at Mosul; one database gives 846 as a minor alternative.
No reliable source found for death year; sources describe him as a mukhadram warrior-poet (fought at al-Qadisiyyah) but give no date of death.

Wikipedia infobox gives 565 CE but several other sources (Wikisource, Wikimedia Commons authority data) give c.544 CE, which is the figure most often cited in secondary literature; pre-Islamic dates are inherently uncertain and traditions disagree (legendary death by poisoned cloak in Ankara).
Multiple sources agree on 7 AH / 629 CE; he lived to see the rise of Islam but did not convert.
110 AH / ~728 CE is the most commonly cited date; one source gives a 101-110 AH range instead of a single year.
Wikipedia and VIAF both give c.696-735 CE / d.117 AH.
Wikipedia explicitly flags the date as uncertain, c.604 CE (605 given as an alternative in some language editions); predates Islam so no AH year.

357 AH consistently cited; killed during a revolt against Sayf al-Dawla's successor. CE conversion given as 967 or 968 depending on source; Turkish encyclopedia gives a specific day in March/April 968.
Multiple independent sources consistently give 168 AH / 784 CE; executed by order of caliph al-Mahdi after satirical verses.
Wikipedia and Britannica both give a disputed range of 712/719 CE; 712 used here as the earlier/more commonly listed figure.
Wikipedia gives c.645/646 CE; Britannica and poets.org only commit to 'after 630 CE'.
c.569 CE is the standard figure (Wikipedia, dbpedia); traditional account has him killed/buried alive in Bahrain on the order of 'Amr ibn Hind.
Wikipedia gives 284 AH / 897 CE, died at Manbij; one bookseller catalogue's 891 CE conversion is inconsistent with 284 AH and treated as an error.
Academic sources (Cambridge journal article, University of Toronto exhibit) give c.649 CE; one gives 647 CE instead.

No reliable source found for an actual death year; a library authority record lists him as 'active 657-704' (an activity span, not a death date), and no biographical source found gives a specific death year.

No reliable source found. Note: do not confuse with the hadith transmitter 'Abu al-Malih al-Hudhali' (d. 101-112 AH), a different person despite the similar name, who turned up repeatedly in searches for this poet.

No reliable source found for a death year. Pre-Islamic; described as nephew of al-Muraqqish al-Akbar and paternal uncle of Tarafa ibn al-'Abd, which places him in roughly the same mid-6th-century CE generation, but no specific year is documented in available sources.
Wikipedia gives 23 September 965 (354 AH); killed in an ambush by bandits near al-Nu'maniyah/Dayr al-'Aqul.

Sources agree only that he died in prison in Mecca during the caliphate of Hisham ibn 'Abd al-Malik (105-125 AH / 724-743 CE); no single year found, so the midpoint of that range is recorded here as a rough approximation, not a sourced exact date.
Wikipedia gives 'c.814 (aged 57-58)' in Baghdad; Britannica gives a slightly wider range of c.813-815; accounts of the circumstances of death vary.
Britannica and academic sources agree on 334 AH / 945 CE; court poet of Aleppo known for nature/garden verse and for an elegy on his daughter Layla.
Wikipedia gives c.650-c.728; Britannica gives 729; a diwan publisher's listing gives the matching 110 AH figure.
Wikipedia gives 13 July 896 in Baghdad; circumstances of death disputed (poisoning vs. illness vs. suicide) but the year is consistent across sources.

Wikipedia gives born 777/died 849 at Homs; one academic source's lifespan (161-236 AH) is roughly consistent, another journal title dates death to 850 CE (234 AH) -- figures differ by about a year across sources.
Single source found (Persian encyclopedia citing al-Zirikli's al-A'lam), giving death in 14 AH after a long life; not independently cross-verified.

Wikipedia and multiple European-encyclopedia authority records (Deutsche Biographie, Store norske leksikon, Bolshaya Rossiyskaya Entsiklopediya) agree on c.701 CE; biographical details are semi-legendary (the 'chaste love' poet of 'Jamil Buthayna').

No reliable source found for a death year; sources (Jawad Ali's al-Mufassal, al-Zirikli's al-A'lam per citation only) describe his legendary 'loyalty' story (refusing to surrender Imru' al-Qais's armor) but none in this search gave a date of death, and some researchers question the story's historicity altogether.

No reliable source found for a specific death year. Wikipedia gives only an era ('late 6th or early 7th century CE'); an old English translation on Wikisource offers two speculative readings (shortly before 569 CE, the year of Muhammad's birth, or sometime in the 40 years between 569 and 609 CE), neither treated as established.

No reliable source found for death year; described as a mukhadram satirist from Najran who settled in Kufa and was threatened by both 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and 'Ali, but no source found gives a date of death.

Only non-Wikipedia secondary sources found; one gives c.743 CE (~125 AH) and explicitly notes the year is disputed in some accounts; not independently cross-verified against a primary biographical source.
No reliable source found for death year; sources describe his conflict with and satire of 'Abbad ibn Ziyad under Umayyad governor 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ziyad, but none found gives a date of death.

Wikipedia and multiple academic sources (SOAS thesis, Iranian Studies Association paper) agree on d. 79 AH; CE conversion given as 698 or 699 depending on source (Hijri year spans two Gregorian years) -- 698 used here, killed in battle in Semnan/Persia.
No reliable source found for death year; biographical dictionaries found describe his lineage and a poem of reproach to Mu'awiya but give no date of death.

Academic sources (Hagemann conference paper and book) consistently give d.703 CE; an Arabic biographical dictionary gives the matching 84 AH; one outlier hadith-transmitter database gives 111 AH, treated as less reliable.

Wikipedia gives c.126 AH/743 CE, killed during the Abbasid Revolution (disputed); National Library of Israel authority record gives 743 or 744 CE depending on reference work (Brockelmann vs. al-Zirikli).

WikiShia gives 68 AH (687-8 CE), drowned in the Euphrates fleeing Mus'ab ibn al-Zubayr's forces; this source describes him primarily as a warrior/political figure rather than explicitly as a poet, so the identification with the corpus's poet of the same name is not independently cross-verified here.

No reliable source found for a specific death year. One source describes him as named after his grandfather Hamduwayh, who carried out the execution of heretics (zandaqa) under Harun al-Rashid (r. 786-809 CE), placing the poet in the early-to-mid Abbasid period, but no death year is given.
Persian-language encyclopedic sources consistently give 'approximately 386 AH' in Aleppo; the 380 AH figure initially checked was not supported by any source found.

A 2024 academic article states that classical biographical literature gives no specific death date for him at all, except al-Zirikli (a modern, late scholar) who places it at approximately 100 AH -- recorded here as the only available figure, explicitly flagged by the source itself as late/secondary.

No source found in this search explicitly states a death year; search results cover his life (ties to the Barmakids, versified Kalila wa-Dimna) but not his death. ~200 AH is a commonly cited figure in general reference works but was not confirmed by a specific citable source in this search -- recorded with low confidence accordingly.
Anonymous/collective attribution ('unknown -- forgotten Abbasid poets'), not an individual -- no individual death year applicable.
Multiple general-reference sources consistently give 161 AH / 777 CE in Baghdad; no academic/primary source was found to cross-verify, hence medium rather than high confidence.
Persian-language sources disagree between c.210 AH and c.220 AH; midpoint (~215 AH / ~830 CE) recorded here as a rough approximation, not a sourced exact date.

No reliable source found. Search results only ever returned information about the major Umayyad poet al-Akhtal (Ghiyath ibn Ghawth al-Taghlibi, d. ~90-92 AH) or about the unrelated pre-Islamic poet 'Ubayd ibn al-Abras -- neither is confirmed as the same person as this corpus entry, and no source describing an 'Ubayd ibn al-Akhtal' was found.

poet_name: عبد الله بن عبد الحميد اللاحقي
note: No reliable source found. Likely related to the attested poet Aban ibn 'Abd al-Hamid al-Lahiqi (same nisba/patronymic pattern), but no source found confirms the relationship or gives any biographical/death information for this specific name.

Multiple academic/bibliographic sources (Sanctum Books, Parnassus Books, a review of Casewit's translation, an Algerian university thesis) consistently give d.690 AH/1291 CE; an initially-checked 688 AH figure was not supported and may reflect confusion with contemporaries such as Fakhr al-Din al-'Iraqi (d.688 AH).

poet_name: المُرَقِّشُ الأكبر (عمرو بن سعد بن مالك)
note: No reliable source found for a death year. One source mentions he worked as a scribe for al-Harith ibn Abi Shamir al-Ghassani 'around 524 CE' (a career anecdote, not a death date, and sourced from only one site); he died before his nephew al-Muraqqish al-Asghar.

Only a single, uncorroborated source found (Arabic Wikisource author page) giving a death of 68 AH; its paired birth date looks implausible and no independent source confirms either figure, so this is recorded as low confidence.
Not an individual poet -- Qur'anic text; no death year applicable.

Wikipedia's Layla and Majnun article and a manuscript-library authority record both give 688 CE, but the historicity of this figure is explicitly disputed in both sources -- likely a legendary/composite figure rather than a precisely documented individual.

No reliable source found for a specific death year; described as a warrior-poet who fought in the Rashidun-era conquests (including against the apostates under Abu Bakr), which places him in the 7th century CE per the site's own period label, but no source found gives an actual death date.
